title: Isolation of mouse Kupffer cells for phenotypic and functional studies
protocol: Euthanize the mouse according to authorized ethical guidelines.
Sanitize the mouse abdomen surface with 70% ethanol.
Cut through the peritoneum, starting with a vertical cut from the lower end of the abdomen to the ribcage.
Perform horizontal cuts at the mid-section of the abdomen to both sides until organs are exposed.
Expose the liver gently without damaging any organs.
Push the intestine right-hand sideward using the blunt end of a forceps to access the liver.
Load a 10 mL syringe with 10 mL of PBS and attach a 27G needle.
Carefully insert the needle into the inferior vena cava and perfuse with 2 mL until the organ starts to swell.
Cut the portal vein using scissors, being careful not to damage the liver.
Continue perfusion until 10 mL of PBS have been injected in about 2 minutes.
Remove the gallbladder.
Cut the liver ligaments connecting the liver to surrounding tissues.
Collect the liver in ice-cold plain RPMI until the next step.
Transfer the liver to a 60 mm Petri dish.
Mince the liver into 1-2 mm³ small pieces using blunt-end scissors.
Transfer liver pieces into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL of pre-warmed ex vivo digestion medium.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Vortex the sample every 10 minutes at 2000 rpm.
Gently homogenize digested liver pieces by forcing them through a 18G needle in a syringe 7-8 times.
Filter the homogenized liver solution through a 70 μm cell strainer into a new 50 mL Falcon tube.
Wash the filter with 10 mL of plain RPMI and transfer to the same Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 50 rcf for 3 minutes.
Discard the aqueous phase and retain the pellet containing dead hepatocytes and debris.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL of ACK buffer and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 30 seconds.
Add 20 mL of plain RPMI to restore osmolarity.
Centrifuge at 400 rcf for 5 minutes.
Discard the top aqueous phase.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of ice-cold plain RPMI.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer into a new 50 mL Falcon tube.
Mix an aliquot of the cell suspension with trypan blue at a ratio of 1:2.
Determine the cell count of viable cells using a Neubauer chamber.
Prime and wash the pump tubes with prewarmed HBSS.
Inject the mouse intravenously with 200 μL of heparin solution (100 Units in PBS) to avoid coagulation issues that can potentially interfere with the perfusion and with the digestion.
Anesthetize the mouse with Avertin (600 μL for a mouse of 25 grams) at 37°C intraperitoneally.
Spread the mouse with 70% EtOH.
Cut through the peritoneum from the lower end of the abdomen to the ribcage vertically.
Perform horizontal cuts at the mid-section of the abdomen to both sides.
Gently push the intestine right-hand sideward using a blunt forceps.
Get access to the liver.
Canulate the inferior vena Cava with a 25G needle.
Optionally, place an open silk suture around the inferior vena Cava.
Start perfusion with Liver Perfusion Medium for 3 min after severing the portal vein.
Perfuse with warm Liver digestion medium for 12 min carefully to avoid air bubbles.
Check liver consistency with a wet cotton applicator starting at 8 min of perfusion.
Once the liver is completely digested, remove the gallbladder.
Cut the liver ligaments connecting the liver to the surrounding tissue.
Transfer the liver into a 60 mm Petri dish with Hepatocyte Wash Medium.
Carefully decapsulate the organ using surgical forceps.
Gently shake the liver while holding it with tweezers.
Transfer the released cell suspension to a 50 mL falcon tube.
Reach a total volume of 50 mL by adding Hepatocyte Wash Medium.
Centrifuge at 20 rcf for 3 minutes.
Collect the pellet enriched in hepatocytes and the soluble fraction containing LNPCs separately.
Resuspend each collected fraction in a separate 15 mL tube with 10 mL of 36% Percoll solution.
Gently mix the resuspended fractions.
Centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 20 minutes without brake.
Discard the Percoll soluble fraction containing cellular debris.
Resuspend hepatocytes in hepatocyte medium and LNPCs in RPMI.
Filter the LNPCs fraction through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Optional: lyse red blood cells with 2 mL of ACK for 30 seconds at 25°C.
Centrifuge and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of RPMI.
Mix an aliquot of each cell suspension 1:2 in trypan blue.
Determine the cell count of viable cells using a Neubauer chamber.
Resuspend LNPCs to a density of 1–3×107/mL in culture medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 100 U/mL Penicillin/Streptomycin.
Plate 1×107 LNPCs per well in a 6-well culture plate.
Incubate the plated cells for 2 h at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Remove cell debris and non-adherent cells by gently washing adherent cells with cold PBS.
Add 50 ng/mL of recombinant M-CSF to the culture medium to maintain Kupffer cell differentiation.
Transfer LNPCs in FACS tubes at a concentration of 5×107/mL for sorting.
Incubate with 200 μL of anti-CD16/CD32 (5 μg/mL in FACS buffer) for 15 min at 4°C.
Wash with 1–2 mL of FACS buffer and spin down for 5 min at 400 rcf.
Incubate with 300 μL of antibody mix for 40 min at 4°C.
Wash with 1–2 mL of FACS buffer and spin down for 5 min at 400 rcf.
Incubate with 200 μL of DAPI (5 μg/mL in FACS buffer) for 5 min at 4°C.
Wash with 1–2 mL of FACS buffer and spin down for 5 min at 400 rcf.
Resuspend in FACS buffer at 5×10^6 cells per mL.
Sort target cells at 4°C using a 100 μm nozzle.
Critical: sheath pressure should not exceed 20 psi to preserve cell viability.
